content.text:
I made three small changes to `0.html`. The stylesheet was already in good shape, so I only fixed gaps I could point to rather than restyling it. I haven't rendered the page in a browser to check the result.

## What changed

- **`<hgroup>` spacing:** a heading inside an `<hgroup>` used to get no top spacing, because it is the first child of its group, and the subtitle sat a full 1rem below the heading. The group now gets the same 2rem above and 1rem below as a bare heading, with the heading and subtitle tight together.
- **`<form>` spacing:** `form` is now in the list of blocks that get a 1rem bottom margin. Before, a form ending in a button or input ran straight into whatever followed it.
- **Print:** headings and heading groups now have `break-inside: avoid`, so a wrapped multi-line heading can't split across pages.

## What I left alone

- **Placeholder content:** the title and `<h1>` are both still "0", and there is no meta description, since I don't know what the page is for.
- **Matters of taste:** I didn't touch things like the 40rem line length, heading sizes (`h4`–`h6` all render at the same size), smooth scrolling or italic `address`.
- **`<header>` inside a later `<article>` or `<section>`:** a heading wrapped this way has the same missing top spacing that `hgroup` had. I didn't fix it because a `header` can hold more than a heading, so the right rule is less clear.
